title: Quantum Optimal Control at Intermediate Times: Controlling Revivals in Spin Chains
authors: Juan J. Omiste, Ignacio R. Solá
abstract: Standard Quantum Optimal Control (QOC) protocols typically maximize a physical objective just at a final target time. However, tracking or measuring the quantum state during the time evolution requires the control at intermediate stages of their evolution. In this work, we extend QOC to accommodate the simultaneous optimization of observables at arbitrary intermediate times. Using a variational approach, we show that intermediate observations induce discontinuities in the costate trajectory, which can be handled with a Krotov algorithm leading to monotonic optimization and convergent results in the limit of zero temporal measurement windows. We apply this multi-time formulation to a Heisenberg XXX spin chain to control the propagation, including field-free revivals, of a Dicke state excitation. Our results demonstrate that simultaneous optimization of the same observable reshapes the driving field to balance intermediate targets with final populations. Finally, we show how this framework enables dynamic tracking of spin excitations and the active manipulation of post-pulse quantum state revivals.
summary: The paper advances Quantum Optimal Control theory by developing methods to optimize quantum observables measured at multiple intermediate times. Using a 5-spin Heisenberg chain model, the authors demonstrate that incorporating these intermediate measurements allows for active manipulation of post-pulse dynamics, successfully controlling quantum state revivals while managing the associated mathematical complexities of costate discontinuities.
main_problem: The work extends Quantum Optimal Control (QOC) protocols to optimize physical observables measured at arbitrary intermediate times, moving beyond standard final-time optimization.
main_result: Simultaneous optimization of multiple intermediate observables reshapes the driving field to balance transient targets with the final population, enabling active manipulation and dynamic tracking of quantum state revivals.
method: A variational approach is used within a Krotov algorithm framework, specifically adapting it to handle discontinuities in the costate trajectory induced by instantaneous (Dirac-delta) intermediate measurements.
model_or_system: The study uses a 5-spin-$1/2$ chain modeled by the Heisenberg XXX Hamiltonian, restricted to the single-excitation manifold. The control is applied via an external time-dependent field $\varepsilon(t)$.
key_observables: Population of the Dicke state $|5angle$, denoted $C_5(t) = |\langle \psi(t)| |5angle|^2$, and the optimal driving field $\varepsilon(t)$.
important_parameters: The measurement window width ($	au$), which is taken to zero for ideal instantaneous measurements, and the penalty factor $\alpha$.
main_assumptions: Standard QOC assumes optimization at a single final time; this work treats intermediate observations as Dirac-delta functions, requiring specialized handling of costate jumps.
figures_summary: Figures compare population dynamics ($|C_5(t)|^2$) for different intermediate measurement times ($T_{int}$) versus standard protocols. The power spectrum (Fig. 4) shows enhanced spectral peaks when intermediate measurements are included.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the limitation of single-time QOC, then develops the theoretical framework to handle multi-time optimization via costate jump conditions and Krotov adaptation. Finally, it applies this method to the spin chain model to demonstrate control over revivals.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it tackles open quantum system dynamics by providing a rigorous mathematical tool (multi-time QOC) to actively steer complex time evolution processes like revival control, which is crucial for quantum memory and simulation.
